title: The Second Quarter: Dream
meter: Prose (the Upaniṣad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pāda and mātrā, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
translation: The second quarter is Taijasa: its field is dream; its awareness turns inward; it has seven limbs and nineteen mouths; and it enjoys the subtle world.
translation_hi: दूसरा पाद तैजस है: उसका क्षेत्र स्वप्न अवस्था है, उसकी चेतना भीतर की ओर है, उसके सात अंग और उन्नीस मुख हैं, और वह सूक्ष्म जगत का भोग करता है।

words.note: From tejas (light), as in Nirvāṇa Ṣaṭkam verse 1.

grammar: Pairs of opposites: बहिष्प्रज्ञ (outward) in mantra 3 and अन्तःप्रज्ञ (inward) here.
Science link: dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is almost as active as when awake, but turned inward, just as the mantra says.
